purpose: Tarvos is a Slicer workflow for myocardial perfusion SPECT/PET. It covers study roles, reorientation to cardiac axes, LV wall detection, stress/rest slices and polar maps, gated QC and review (thickening, motion, EF), and DICOM export of screens and scenes. It targets nuclear medicine users.
summary: I read the CMake files, MPIGated.py, widgets.py, the module class of MyocardialPerfusionImaging.py, and parts of toolbar.py and dicomexport.py. A search of the whole module folder found no pip installs, subprocess calls, network access, pickle, eval or exec. The MIT license is present and the dependencies match between the catalog entry and EXTENSION_DEPENDS. The main problem is packaging. The CMake resource list names `Resources/Images/banner.jpg`, but the committed file is `Banner.jpg`. On case-sensitive build machines (Linux, probably macOS) this can break the build or the banner. The logo.png listed in the hints was not visible in the file listing, which showed only Banner.jpg. I did not read most of the remaining large modules. No clinical-use disclaimer was checked.
not_checked: Most of the code of MPIProcessing, MPIMyocardium, MPIReview, MPIGatedQC, MPIDataRoles and Lib/myocardium, display and parameters was not read line by line; I relied on a regex search for dangerous calls.
Whether Resources/Images/logo.png and Branding/Tarvos_logo.png exist (large files not readable).
Whether the build succeeds in practice, and the DICOMSpectRecon and PET4D dependencies.
Clinical-use disclaimer in the README and module help.
Whether the revision `main` resolves to commit 1362f85.
questions_for_author: Is the resource file `banner.jpg` or `Banner.jpg`, and is `Resources/Images/logo.png` committed? Does the build pass on Linux?
Do you plan to pin scm_revision to a commit or tag?
